question: Does the signed momentum retained by a stationary mouth survive true discharge, and how much ordinary inflow mechanically participates?

held_geometry.carrier_boundary: Reflecting round lip, collar and flare join an open disk and a reflecting plane outside the disk. The downstream region in the ordinary carrier problem extends to r=9 and w=10.

interpretation.ordinary_carrier: Stationary first-order dipole of the finite-domain carrier, driven by far-brane speed U, with unforced receiving reservoir. Positive F/U is carrier-on-rigid-wall; external holder reacts oppositely. Advection, amplitude-gradient stress and isotropic stress included. All 15 nested budgets contain the feeding boundary, receiving plane (inner and outer) and cylindrical side. Reversals/halving are checks of linear equations. Tiny receiving net stress is below the global closure residual. Physical identification of the reflecting support with free material is an independent assumption.
interpretation.tagged_stream: Independent incident sideways speed specified at the local injection section. Warm radial speed is Gaussian at surface equilibrium radius with quadrature over ±9 standard deviations. The mathematical well persists on both sides of R(w) with the unmodified native positive order tail and prescribed w clock. Angular slip is free. Equality of opposite force/impulse is verified by integrating acceleration projected onto the lab direction separately from the laboratory momentum at each cut. The pressureless tags have kinetic momentum export and contact force only. For the exit partition, the total signed outgoing flux is accumulated over inner disk and exterior annulus separately for each drive. No release law is implied by the exterior flux. Information beyond the aperture is missing for this preparation. Angularly and radially finite quadrature samples cannot prove a universal zero admission probability.
interpretation.guide_control: Explicit new candidate. Constant inner radial offset, normal accommodation at the entry, angle-free sliding on a prescribed radial cross-sectional guide with w(t) imposed, then force-free flight past receiver planes. A single holder takes both inlet and guide impulses. The relative radial energy removed includes the undriven thermal energy and an incremental U²/6. This is not a fully free four-dimensional collision, nor a calibration of the true wall or a continuation of the Morse run. The initial 1/3 fraction would belong to a different object if its accommodation were borne elsewhere.
interpretation.ordinary_participation: Measured stationary axisymmetric carrier current within stated radial distances from the wall. Flux-rank extrema describe sampled geometric opportunities under ideal conserved throughflow and ordering; the finite-element residual matters especially in the last 0.05 mouth radii. There is no independent bound-site occupancy or normal attachment law. Doubling the noninteracting tag population doubles its assigned load at the same per-tag response. Only distinct physical populations may be summed. The tagged fraction and carrier load use different velocity references and receivers.

numerical_notes: Cold signed ancillary control emitted overflow/invalid warnings in internal DOP853 evaluations; recorded accepted states were finite and obeyed the momentum test. The thermal and carrier claims use runs with empty stderr plus independent linear radial checks.

The finite source-velocity quadrature converges more slowly than the lab distribution shift. Report only approximate unrestricted plateau; the aperture test is the robust observable. Initial formatting/CLI trials stopped before physics output and do not contribute readings.
scientific_decision: The ordinary carrier satisfies a stationary held-force and boundary-balance test. The original Morse-tag channel fails to traverse the modeled opening. A separate explicit constraint can sustain a force, conditional on capture, axial steering, and support. Multiplying proximity current or the external speed by the old 32.18% cannot calibrate the model. Free acceleration, matching support to the physical mouth and radius universality remain open.

independent_reviews.verdict: Scoped clear for positivity of the archived quadratic wall-order tail and the unrestricted smooth-well momentum plateau. On both audited meshes every sampled warm zero-drift trajectory missed the finite discharge aperture. The plateau gives a conditional force on the imposed potential and leaves the post-discharge mouth reaction unmeasured.

independent_reviews.scope: Carrier stress integration and ordinary influx
independent_reviews.verdict: Scoped clear for the rigid reflecting carrier’s signed pressure reaction and nested total momentum balances at their stated resolution, and for the sampled ordinary proximity currents. These measurements do not give the load borne by a freely supported mouth or an independently measured contact fraction.

independent_reviews.scope: Discharge, ordinary carrier and the alternative sliding guide
independent_reviews.verdict: Scoped clear for the direct weak signed lateral momentum balance of the unrestricted shell, for the separate held rigid carrier’s pressure and control-surface ledger, and for the aperture-admitted angular-slip guide under its specified axial drive. The first shell leaves the fluid domain; the alternative imposes bilateral radial retention and shifts the launch ring inward by the guide clearance. Ordinary proximity current, tag normalization and the kinetic loss on radial capture do not determine actual participating mass, support routing or free-mouth acceleration.

Scoped clear for the held reflecting carrier’s signed force and nested stress balances, the sampled ordinary proximity currents, the original tags’ failure to enter the outlet, and the guide’s conditional momentum transfer with prescribed axial motion. None of these measurements fixes the physical attached population, transfer to a mobile mouth, or free-fall acceleration.

import sys,json
from pathlib import Path
import numpy as np
sys.path.insert(0,str(Path('software/stage1_solver/tools').resolve()))
from mouth_middle_tag_grip import cubic_trace
from mouth_flared_receiver import EXIT
for mesh in (26,34):
    tr,rate=cubic_trace(mesh)
    cells=[]
    for w0,w1,(left,mid,right) in zip(tr.edges[:-1], tr.edges[1:], tr.chi, strict=True):
        if w1<1.427: continue
        a=2*(left+right-2*mid); b=4*mid-3*left-right
        roots=np.roots([a,b,left])
        extrema=[(0.,left),(1.,right)]
        v=-b/(2*a) if a else -1.
        if 0<v<1: extrema.append((v,(a*v+b)*v+left))
        mn=min(extrema,key=lambda p:p[1]); mx=max(extrema,key=lambda p:p[1])
        cells.append({'lo':w0,'hi':w1,'min':mn[1],'wmin':w0+(w1-w0)*mn[0],'max':mx[1],'roots':[float(w0+(w1-w0)*r.real) for r in roots if r.imag==0 and 0<=r.real<1]})
    print(json.dumps(dict(mesh=mesh,rate=rate,exit=EXIT,end_order=tr.chi[-1,-1],extrema=min(cells,key=lambda c:c['min']),first_zero=next((c for c in cells if c['roots']),None),negative_cells=sum(1 for c in cells if c['min']<0),tail=[(float(w),float(tr.sample(tr.chi,w)[0])) for w in [1.55,1.65,1.8,2.,2.25,2.5,2.7,2.85,3.,EXIT]],clocks=[(float(w),float(tr.transit(1.175,w,8))) for w in [1.55,2.,2.5,3.,EXIT]])))

"""Aperture classification of the native wall-centered tag model. The Gaussian score includes
the motion of the aperture selection when differentiating incident drift."""
import sys,json
from pathlib import Path
import numpy as np
from scipy.integrate import solve_ivp
from scipy.special import roots_legendre
sys.path.insert(0,str(Path('software/stage1_solver/tools').resolve()))
from mouth_middle_tag_grip import cubic_trace
from mouth_calibrated_flare_coating import read_inputs
from neutral_patch_sites import BETWEEN,TEMPERATURE
from mouth_segment_contact_hold import PITCH
from mouth_flared_receiver import EXIT
mesh,n=map(int,sys.argv[1:])
tr,rate=cubic_trace(mesh)
lo=1.175
patch,*_=read_inputs(mesh)
scale=2*patch['shared_scale']
D,alpha,_=BETWEEN
sigma=np.sqrt(scale*TEMPERATURE)
t,wgt=roots_legendre(n); t*=9.; wgt*=np.exp(-.5*t*t); wgt/=wgt.sum()
z=sigma*t; R0,Rp=tr.geometry.radius(lo)
y=np.zeros((3,n)); y[0]=R0; y[1]=Rp*tr.speed(lo)+z
were_outside=np.zeros(n,bool); were_deep=np.zeros(n,bool)
cuts=np.array([tr.crossing(.01),1.55,1.8,2.,2.25,2.5,2.75,2.95,EXIT])
edges=np.unique(np.r_[lo,tr.edges[(tr.edges>lo)&(tr.edges<EXIT)],cuts])
for left,right in zip(edges[:-1],edges[1:]):
    j=np.searchsorted(tr.edges,.5*(left+right))-1
    e0,e1=tr.edges[j:j+2]; width=e1-e0
    ca,cm,cb=tr.chi[j]; pa,pm,pb=tr.psi[j]
    A,B=2*(ca+cb-2*cm),4*cm-3*ca-cb
    P,Q=2*(pa+pb-2*pm),4*pm-3*pa-pb
    def ode(w,Y):
        r,v,_=Y.reshape(y.shape)
        R,Rp=tr.geometry.radius(w)
        b=(w-e0)/width
        chi=(A*b+B)*b+ca
        psi=(P*b+Q)*b+pa
        u=((2*b*P+Q)/(psi*width)).imag/(1+Rp*Rp)
        # Multiply in logarithmic form so true restoring forces remain resolved at tiny χ.
        if chi<=0 or u<=0: raise ArithmeticError('negative order or inflow')
        e=alpha*(R-r)/PITCH; L=np.log(chi)
        acc=scale*(2*D*alpha/PITCH)*(np.exp(L+2*e)-np.exp(L+e))
        return (np.array([v,acc,1/r**2])/u).ravel()
    sol=solve_ivp(ode,(left,right),y.ravel(),method='DOP853',rtol=2e-9,atol=2e-12,dense_output=False)
    if not sol.success: raise ArithmeticError(sol.message)
    states=sol.y.reshape(3,n,-1)
    radii=tr.geometry.radius(sol.t)[0]
    were_outside|=np.max(states[0]-radii,axis=1)>1e-8
    were_deep|=np.min(states[0]-radii,axis=1)<-PITCH
    y=states[:,:,-1].copy()
    if right in cuts:
        r,v,I=y
        R,Rp=tr.geometry.radius(right)
        inside=r<=R
        angular=R0/r+R0*v*I
        rad=z*v/(sigma*sigma)
        response=(rad+2*angular)/3
        gap=r-R
        print(json.dumps(dict(mesh=mesh,n=n,cut=right,R=R,chi=tr.sample(tr.chi,right)[0],mass_in=wgt@inside,mass_out=wgt@(~inside),ever_out=wgt@were_outside,ever_compressed_one_pitch=wgt@were_deep,radial_cap=1-wgt@response,export_in=wgt@(response*inside),export_out=wgt@(response*(~inside)),gap_range=[gap.min(),gap.max()],radial_speed_range=[v.min(),v.max()],max_tailscore= max(abs(rad[0]),abs(rad[-1]))),default=lambda value: np.asarray(value).item()),flush=True)
